question: Do the archived row boundaries on LP2-00–55 produce more prime-valued Gematria Primus row sums than within-page rune shuffles?
representation: Each nonempty archived text line with at least one recognized rune defines one row. Include headings. Remove non-alphabet characters; ignore rows with no recognized runes. No corrections or decryption.
statistic: Total number of rows with a prime sum across all selected pages. One global statistic; per-page counts are descriptive only.
null: Independently permute the full rune multiset within each page, then partition it using that page’s original row lengths. Preserve page counts and every row length, not words or per-row counts.
tail: greater than or equal, including ties
monte_carlo_p: (1 + shuffled totals at least observed) / (1 + trials)
stopping_rule: Evaluate all 56 pages and 999 full-dataset shuffles. Retain observed row sums and all per-page null counts. No early stopping.
exclusions: Emirps, prime ordinals, decoded text, arbitrary regions, changed spellings, other boundaries and page-specific significance claims.
limitations: Pages, statistic and null are analyst choices motivated by existing prime-sum discussion, not a blind discovery. No correction for earlier or future alternative analyses.
